newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine traders expect well-bid Letes sale Tues.
newsitem.headline: Argentine traders expect well-bid Letes sale Tues.

text.p: Argentine market players said Monday the monthly Treasury bill (Letes) auction on Tuesday will be well bid given the abundant liquidity in the market.
"The auction will go well. There is a lot of liquidity around and money market rates are low," said the chief trader at an Argentine bank.
The Economy Ministry will auction 250 million pesos of 91-day bills and 250 million pesos of 182-day debt.

An analyst at a foreign bank said: "I don't think these issues are a big deal, especially in the light of the $2 billion (global bond) issue." He was referring to the global issue Argentina will place before the end of January.
Another trader pointed out that since this is Argentina's first debt placement of the year it should be closely watched.
Market watchers' forecast a discount rate from a low of 6.50 percent to a higher of 7.13 percent on the 91-day Letes issue. Most of the players polled by Reuters saw a discount rate of 6.75 percent.

The last peso issue of 91-day Letes, in November, fetched a discount rate of 7.60 percent. The lowest rate ever received on 91-day peso bills since Argentina began the Letes program in April was in May 1996 at 5.70 percent.
As for the 182-day peso-denominated bills, players forecasts ranged from 7.0 percent to 7.80 percent. Most saw the discount rate at 7.5 percent.
Tuesday's sale of 182-day peso Letes is only the second time under the program that Argentina auctions 182-day peso bills. The last time, in July 1996, the offering garnered a rate of 7.32 percent.
Offers for the issues are due by 1400 local time/1200 EST/1700 GMT Tuesday. The sale takes place through Dutch style auction and settlement is due on January 17.
